title: Cross-region tail-latency cliff from bursty streaming clients - postmortem and mitigation plan
creator: Asha Patel
summary: A sudden surge of long-lived streaming requests originating from a batch analytics job in Secondary region caused cascading tail-latency degradation across Primary and Secondary. Circuit breaker misfires and aggressive load-shedding rules interacted poorly, triggering regional failovers and degraded SLOs for 22 minutes. This ticket captures timeline, root cause, mitigations taken, and follow-up actions.
description: What happened: At 2026-03-05T01:13:00Z we observed a rapid increase in 95th/99th percentile latency across inference serving in both us-west-2 (Primary) and eu-west-1 (Secondary). Within three minutes, a set of region-local circuit breakers tripped due to sustained per-shard queue depth, which triggered cross-region failover policies. Failover amplified load imbalances (hot-shard concentration and KV cache misses), producing a persistent latency cliff and SLO miss lasting ~22 minutes for customers on affected tenants. Severity: P0 — multiple customers hit 99th percentile latency SLOs and one high-volume customer reported application errors.
timeline: 01:13:00Z - Metrics: sudden uptick in active streaming sessions in eu-west-1 from internal analytics pool (spike ~9x baseline).
01:14:20Z - Per-shard queues in eu-west-1 start exceeding safe thresholds; 95th latency rises.
01:15:05Z - Local region circuit breakers (short-window) transition to open for several shards.
01:15:30Z - Smart routing policy fails over subset of traffic to us-west-2 causing hot-shard amplification and KV cache cold misses.
01:16:10Z - Control plane heartbeats for a set of dedicated workers show jitter; autoscaler starts conservative scale-up.
01:17:00Z - Global graded-degradation kicks in; tiered load-shedding begins with aggressive eviction of long-running streams.
01:23:00Z - Circuit hysteresis timers reset after backups and autoscale provisions additional capacity.
01:35:15Z - Metrics return to baseline; incident declared mitigated.
impact: Multiple customers experienced 95th/99th percentile latency SLO breaches for up to 22 minutes. Some long-lived streaming connections were evicted by load-shedding leading to application errors and retried traffic, which increased cost. Internal telemetry shows increased token counts and Kafka backlog for analytics ingesters during the event.
root_cause: Three-way interaction between (1) a synthetic burst of long-lived streaming sessions generated by an internal analytics job in Secondary region, (2) short-window circuit breaker hysteresis tuned to protect single-shard tail latency but not aware of cross-region re-routing, and (3) routing fallback that moved stateful in-flight streaming traffic to Primary where KV cache warmed slowly. The combination produced hot shards, KV cache cold misses, and a feedback loop with shedding that amplified load rather than containing it.
contributing_factors: Internal analytics job lacked rate-limits and used production inference endpoints in eu-west-1 during a maintenance window.
Circuit breaker short-window thresholds (10s) were tuned for transient spikes but caused oscillation under sustained long-lived sessions.
Smart-routing policy favored immediate failover without shard-aware redistribution, concentrating traffic on a subset of replicas.
KV cache warmup is single-threaded per-shard; moving streams to a new shard incurred cold-cache latency penalties.
Observability smoothing windows were too aggressive, delaying detection of long-tail buildup until SLOs were already breached.
mitigations_taken: 01:16Z - Throttled internal analytics job at the source via service account policy (temporary block).
01:17Z - Relaxed immediate failover policy to prefer degraded local serving with soft-rate limits for long-running streams (temporary config change).
01:18Z - Increased circuit breaker hysteresis windows from 10s to 30s to avoid rapid oscillation (hotfix).
01:19Z - Triggered expedited autoscale for affected pools and added two cold-standby replicas to absorb failover traffic.
immediate_actions: Disable production access for known analytics job IDs until job is updated (owner: DataEng - Priya Shah) - due 2026-03-06
Hotfix CB hysteresis reverted to safer config if oscillation detected (owner: Marco Rivera) - action completed 2026-03-05
Add temporary routing guard to avoid redirecting >20% of in-flight streaming tokens off a shard within 60s window (owner: SRE - Noah Kim) - due 2026-03-07
long_term_actions: Implement shard-aware failover logic: routing engine must be replica/shard-aware and maintain relative load balance during cross-region failover (owner: Serving Runtime - Mei Wong) - due 2026-04-15
Introduce probabilistic soft-shedding for long-lived streams instead of deterministic eviction; allow graceful reconnect with warm-cache hints (owner: Runtime - Alex Johnson) - due 2026-05-01
KV cache parallel warmup: allow background prefetch across replicas on failover to eliminate single-threaded warm path (owner: Runtime - Alex Johnson) - due 2026-05-01
Add a dedicated telemetry signal for long-lived stream density per shard and a rapid-alert for >3x baseline with 2-minute detection SLA (owner: Observability - Lina Gomez) - due 2026-03-22
Create a canary + chaos test harness that simulates long-lived streaming job bursts and verifies routing + CB interactions before rollout (owner: SRE - Noah Kim) - due 2026-04-01

Formalize internal sandbox controls: deny-list production endpoint usage by internal batch/analytics jobs and enforce a posture review for any job that requires production inference (owner: Security - Omar Diaz) - due 2026-03-20
postmortem_notes: We observed that deterministic load-shedding that evicted long-lived sessions caused retried traffic which concentrated load on a smaller set of shards; probabilistic shedding could have reduced requeue hotspots.

Circuit breaker hysteresis must be evaluated in the context of routing policies; small-window CBs that cause rapid open/close behave well for ephemeral spikes but are harmful when traffic becomes long-lived.
Autoscale is slow for head-of-line long-lived streams; need pre-provisioning heuristics for bursty long-duration workloads (e.g., pre-warm lanes for streaming clients).

notes_for_future_incidents: Avoid immediate cross-region evacuation of in-flight stateful streams. Prefer local degraded serving with soft-throttles and tag in-flight connections for cache warmup hints. Ensure internal jobs cannot use production inference endpoints without explicit rate-limited proxy.
